questions: Did the four party members first meet while gambling with a man who turned out to be cheating them?
Did they take the cheating gambler's treasure map after discovering his deception?
Did Uriah use his once-a-day ability to speak with aquatic animals to talk to Reginald the frog?
Did Uriah learn from Reginald the frog about the Clurichen, a creature that comes out of the river each night to cause mischief in town?
Did the party enter Brandonsford and choose to go into the Clumsy Fox Tavern rather than the nearly abandoned inn across from it?
Did they meet the Clumsy Fox's halfling owner, Bentley?
Did they meet the noblewoman Lady Hilda at the Clumsy Fox?
Did they meet Drop Dead Ned, a thief who carries a killer wasp in a tiny jar, at the Clumsy Fox?
Did Drop Dead Ned broker a deal to be hired by the party for 100 gold a week, paying them back each time they let him kill someone?
Did Eric the Reeve tell the party that a dragon was plaguing the countryside and that the town offers 1000 gold to whoever slays it?
Did Eric the Reeve recommend that the party talk to George the hunter, who had lost his arm to the dragon?
Did the party learn the legend that centuries ago the warrior Sir Brandon received a magic sword from a fairy and used it to slay a dragon terrorizing the village?
Did the party learn that Sir Brandon was knighted and had the town named after him before he eventually left?
Did Dunk befriend Farmer Gill, who knows the tale of Sir Brandon by heart?
Did Farmer Gill try to sell Dunk his mule Seamus for 100 gold?
Did Farmer Gill's sons leave town to try to kill the dragon?
Did the party meet Quinn, the owner of the Golden Egg Tavern, whose liquor is terrible and far more expensive than the Clumsy Fox's?
Did Quinn, believing Bentley was stealing his good wine shipments, offer 100 gold to whoever caught the thief?
Has no alcohol shipments reached the town for weeks because of the dragon, leaving supplies running low?
Had no one actually seen or heard the dragon except, supposedly, George the hunter?
Was Sir Phidipaldi thrown out of the Clumsy Fox after challenging the town's reeve to a duel?
Is Dunk a trollkin wanderer exiled from his own people?
Does Dunk carry a pack full of odd, occasionally useful trinkets, reflecting his knowledge of weird items?
Is Trout a river halfling who fights with a sling and spear?
Can Trout stand nearly unseen when he remains unmoving?
Is Sir Phidipaldi a human errant fool who became enamored with chivalric tales and is often wrong about what he knows?
Does Sir Phidipaldi carry a two-handed sword named Sir Chumunga and a lance named Lady Isaboob?
Is Dr Uriah a Dagonite metaphysician who can breathe underwater, speak with aquatic animals once a day, and sense the tides?
Did Uriah end up carrying the party's treasure map?
Did Dunk scout Warwick the smith's shop at night while it was closed?
Did Dunk personally see a magical mithril chain shirt glinting in the window of Warwick's shop?
Did Uriah stake out the river at night hoping to follow the Clurichen?
Did Sir Phidipaldi sleep in the Golden Egg's basement and scatter marbles across the floor to try to catch the alcohol thief?
Did Dunk discover that the sheepish woman he saw near Warwick's house was actually Ingrid the alchemist?
Did Ingrid confess to Dunk that she secretly leaves gifts on Warwick's windowsill at night?
Did Ingrid confess to Dunk that she likes to watch Warwick sleep?
Did Ingrid grow suspicious of Dunk's motives and refuse to let him into Warwick's house at first?
Did Dunk propose that Ingrid brew a sleeping potion so she could watch Warwick without fear of him waking?
Did Ingrid say she needed faun wine from a grove across the river as an ingredient for the sleeping potion?
Did Dunk agree to fetch faun wine and meet Ingrid again the next night at the same spot and time?
Did the invisible Clurichen drag a jug across the river and then turn invisible?
Did Trout and Uriah follow the invisible creature's footprints to the Golden Egg Tavern's basement?
Did the party capture the Clurichen, who identified himself as Naggeneen?
Did Quinn take custody of the captured Naggeneen and pay 33 gold each to Trout, Uriah, and Sir Phidipaldi as the promised reward?
Did the group discuss rolling specific dice (such as D6 or D20) to determine whether an action succeeded?
Was a numeric target number or threshold (e.g., needing to roll a 14 or higher, or beating an armor class of 15) discussed as part of resolving an action?
Did the group discuss saving throws and a bonus (such as a +2 poison resistance for trollkin) as a game mechanic?
Did the group discuss an optional "fumble" rule for ranged attacks accidentally hitting an ally on a roll of one?
Was there discussion of experience points, leveling up, or gaining a mechanical follower as game procedure?
Did participants make out-of-character jokes or comments referencing real-world sports (such as the Mariners and Phillies)?

Did participants make out-of-character jokes or references to real-world media, stereotypes, or other games (such as Water World, Call of Cthulhu dice, Blades in the Dark, or comments about yarmulkes and horns)?
Did particpants discuss using Call of Cthulhu dice?
Did participants discuss stories about thier rabbi being asked to remove his yarmulke?
Was there meta-commentary about the game system's rules design, such as noting it uses fixed odds rather than difficulty numbers?
Did the group discuss which character classes exist in the ruleset (such as fighter, magic-user, and cleric) as a game system note?
Was a character's Dexterity or Charisma score mentioned as a numeric stat to determine an action's outcome?
